    Age 7 — Human Age

    The Era of Moderate Prosperity¶

    Age 7 was not a golden age like the Dwarf Era. It was an era of moderate prosperity — stable, functional, but never spectacular. The post-Romanium economy had found its equilibrium. Trade routes were established. Cities grew. Populations recovered from the wars of the Iron Age.

    The Three Great Empires¶

    By 1500 BGD, three great empires dominated the known world — two human, one beastmen:

    • The Old Lumina Empire (Lumina Continent) — the largest, controlling territory from the northern mountains to the southern coast. Built and ruled by the civilized beastmen of the age, and founded by Emperor Kaelor I — a beastman — in 1729 BGD, who unified the Lumina city-states through a combination of strategic marriage, calculated war, and an administrative genius not matched since the Dwarf Era.
    • The Grimmel Federation (northern Erisdar) — a loose alliance of countist lords who valued autonomy over empire. Its founder, Lord-Protector Armin Grimmel, rejected the imperial model explicitly, establishing the countist principles that would endure for 3,000 years.
    • The Tabontabar Dynasty (Tabontabar) — isolationist, sea-protected, culturally distinct. Ruled by the Zhao lineage, who claimed descent from the Glorious Alliance's original command crew. They traded with outsiders but never conquered.

    These three empires maintained an uneasy balance. Wars were frequent but limited — border skirmishes, trade disputes, succession crises. No empire could defeat the other two, and none tried.

    The Rot Within¶

    But beneath the surface, rot was spreading.

    The institutions of the great empires became beyond repair — corrupt. The empires that had conquered continents could not govern themselves. Officials sold offices. Judges sold verdicts. Generals sold their loyalty. The centralization that had made the age's great powers powerful was also making it fragile.

    The Shadows, working through homunculi agents and willing collaborators, manipulated this corruption. They did not cause it — they merely accelerated it. A bribe here. A whispered suggestion there. A convenient natural disaster that destroyed a key city. The empire did not fall from one blow. It eroded from within.

    Countism's Birth¶

    Countism emerged as a political philosophy during the mid-Age 7 as a direct response to imperial overreach. Lord-Protector Armin Grimmel codified its principles in the Compact of Grimmel (2412 BGD):

    • Lords hold their own territory. No imperial governor may override a local lord's decree.
    • Castles are the unit of power. Not capitals. Not courts. The castle on the hill answers to no one but its lord.
    • Central authority is suggestion, not command. Kings may call for war. Lords may decline.

    Countism spread rapidly. It was inefficient — every castle had its own laws, its own taxes, its own army. But it was resilient. When empires collapsed, countist regions survived. When Baoth rose, countist lords resisted. When the Shadows tried to centralize Ge'or, they found countism waiting for them — a system that could not be co-opted because it had no center to capture.

    Cultural Foundations¶

    Age 7 established the cultural bedrock of modern Ge'or:

    • Most modern religions were created during this age. The pantheons, the rituals, the sacred texts — all date from the Human Age. The Erisian church would later overlay, co-opt, or suppress many of them, but they were born here.
    • Languages stabilized. The linguistic chaos of earlier ages settled into the forms that are still spoken today. Changes since Age 7 have been minor — regional dialects, borrowed words, but the core structures are the same. A modern Baothian speaker could understand an Age 7 human with little difficulty.
    • Art and philosophy flourished. The Imperial Academy of Kaelor produced the Meditations on Empire — a treatise on governance that the Shadows would later suppress. The Grimmel poets wrote the Songs of the Free Lords, still sung in countist territories. The Zhao scholars compiled the Tabontabar Histories, the oldest continuous written record on Ge'or outside the Archive.

    Sytrenis and the Catmen¶

    The Human Age was also the age of the catmen's near-extinction — and of the hero who ended it. Born in 1667 BGD, Masaaki Sytrenis at twenty-two (~1645 BGD) saved the xenophobic kingdom of Termopolas from the waking Metrak, a mountain-sized war-machine of the Last Great War hidden in the region of the now-Erisian Empire. The great epic of that adventure, the Great Epic of the Heroes of Donblond'werv, records how he stopped the machine, endured the Tunwif–Termopolas conflict that followed, and — as "Sytrenis the Diplomat" — ended the persecution that gave birth to the Lesser Catmen. His deeds are the foundation of Sytrenis, the most ancient catmen religion.

    The Fall — The Last War of Humanity¶

    The age ended not with a whimper but with a war.

    In 967 BGD, the empire of Baoth — under the dragon king Goldenborn — rose to power. What had begun as a dragon-ruled city-state in earlier ages had grown into a political and military force. Goldenborn was not yet possessed by the Shadows; his early reign was genuinely enlightened. But the Shadow presence in his court was already deep.

    With human institutions corroded beyond salvation, Baoth swept through the weakened empires in a conflict known as "the last war of humanity." The Old Lumina Empire was the first to fall. The Grimmel Federation held longer than any — countism's decentralized nature made it difficult to conquer — but even the free lords could not withstand the dragon's armies indefinitely.

    The continent-spanning empires — human and beastmen alike — collapsed. The age of great empires was over. Age 8 — the Age of Baoth — had begun.

    Connections¶

    50–100 Year Transition¶

    Baoth's victory inaugurated Age 8 — Age of Baoth — a kingdom that was, paradoxically, the most multi-species state in Ge'or's history. Human institutions crumbled. A dragon ruled. But the people in the streets were elves, dwarves, demons, and former Donblond'werv citizens who had simply... stayed.
